consequence.statement: Resource tracking will switch from label-based to annotation-based tracking on the next sync operation; labels will be replaced with annotations, and applications will not be marked as out-of-sync if labels are not present on resources.
consequence.remediation: Verify that annotation-based tracking is compatible with your environment. Monitor the first sync operation after upgrade for potential edge cases with resource deletion that may cause resources to be orphaned.

original.statement: The default value of the application.resourceTrackingMethod configuration in the argocd-cm ConfigMap changes from label-based tracking to annotation-based tracking in Argo CD 3.0.

decision.reason: [ev-07e8b4d1d6f1] (the 2.14→3.0 upgrade guide) says the default tracking method changes from label to annotation for anyone with application.resourceTrackingMethod unset or set to label. The change text from the same section says that for most users the upgrade is safe, labels are replaced with annotations on the next sync, and applications are not marked out-of-sync. That means things keep working but behave differently, so behavior-change (review) fits. Orphaned resources are described only as a known edge case: when the first sync after the switch deletes a resource. That is a risk to verify, not a stated failure for exposed environments, so the medium severity and the remediation about monitoring the first sync fit; note the shown excerpt itself is cut off before the remediation and warning.
